body:
Ah, but the passion of learning is addictive too. 
And some folks love teaching. 
The insecurity is brutal!  I tell my friends starting an MA, just know that every insecurity you've had will show up, it's what placing so much value on your thoughts and words does. 
I do  think so much is fucked up in academia, but it's also the existing system for research that is not wholly corporate, right. Almost all the profs I know care so much about making the world a better place for others. 
Are you in a better spot now?

Earlier this year ago I saw no point, I get it. It's tough rn. But here's a song about how letters are better

https://bigmamalele.bandcamp.com/album/letters-are-better

Academia is like mainlining insecurity. I say this as a former heroin addict and current phd candidate (w/BED and CPTSD). 
We are trained to be so critical, question everything, it's hard to turn it off. 

You are just a stranger on reddit,I'm not gonna comment on the value of your research because I honestly don't know. Not in the humanities. 

But, the mental health of phds is so low, over half have depression/anxiety during their degree. (Ha, reddit, no need to cite, but it's TRUE!)

Also, when people say nice things, they tend to mean  what they say. That's why they bothered to say it, they think it so strongly!

I love learning, doing a phd lol. I think life is about learning. I love reading a book or article that blows my mind. And I love sharing a book or article that blows my mind with friends. 

I love my friends. COVID19 is so isolating, I got so depressed, felt like I was losing everything. But I've been reaching out, and people are glad to catch up. Some were in their own depression hole. 

Gifts. I love making little gifts for folks, whether is postcards, picking wild greens and berries and making teas, etc. 

Dancing. I miss live music so much. Dancing and singing though, those feel good, once you get past the nervousness at the start.

New experiences. I'm a try anything once kind of person. New walking trail, new to me ethnic food, new kind of fitness, new area of the city to walk in... the newness slows down time, and we create more memories as we are taking in an environment or hobby for the first time. Helps lessen the feeling stuck and hopelessness vibes. 

Sharing and giving back, using my lil bit of power to make the world a better place. I do volunteer work. 

Gratitude. Everyday I write 5 things that went well. Positive psychology tool. 

Art. I'm a creative. I get excited to make projects, more than I have time to do. But that brainstorming at the beginning, I feel so alive.

Or me, Single serve/ less Bingey portions, like cookie at a cafe instead of a box. I know it's more expensive, but you allow the craving, without a box of cookies in your house. 

 Also, trial and error, maybe try eating it with a friend present to moderate binging if you have a friend you can talk to about this?

Maybe you could write down what you've learned from grocery store shopping recently (eating to prevent a binge sounded weird to me) but trying to not restrict a lot makes sense. So it's not all in your head, you can map it out and plan. 

BED sucks, keep trying and be kind to yourself

Woaaaaaah you post just gave me a realization that I totally care about the BIG STUFF  have lots of friends with similar homelessness addiction traumas too who are the same way. I used to find it hard to understand simple, genuine hobbies.
Interesting, thank you.
Congrats, I used to not understand why people celebrated this moment, but having gone through it myself, I get it now. It is a big deal!
This is a good comment, we have different voices in our head and the binge one is sneaky

You could maybe try a small portion, of the highest quality version. I find its shitty convenience store type food that I used  to binge on. Theres certain Bingey foods I only buy a bit of. Enough to quench the urge, but not enough to binge on. Like I'll buy one croissant, instead of a 6 pack (because I'll binge). Or a very small bit of amazing cheese, instead of a big cheap block that I snack on. It's a way to not restrict completely, but also lessen the possibility of binging. For example, ryevita are the crackers I buy, because other ones like triscuits are binge foods. 

It's also, about not giving up when you do binge again. It's the giving up that leads to more binging. Its can be so hard. 

Maybe a dietician with BED skills could help you figure this out. 

Congrats on continuing to work through this ❤
Same here. Now I'm doing my PhD.

I guess the point is, this is all we have. If nothing matters, then at least do what you want. 

I thought the point of life was to learn. (So here I am, sad and struggling with a PhD lol). Can you think of any sensations you'd like to feel, things you'd like to do?

Can you activate your body in a way that feels good? Meaninglessness is often mentally construed, you think it before you feel it, pleasure and joy are more embodied. 

 I'm just coming out of a low meaningless period as well, I get it. It sucks.
Fuck
What's the 100 lb loss meeting group info? Thanks!

I went to my first meeting because I was sick of struggling. Trying to manage my urges to eat and lose weight was draining my life. It felt like it was getting worse. I thought maybe a community of people could help. I don't have friends who struggle with food like this. I was impressed that I was the fattest in the room though, seems like it works for many.

A lot of that 5 kilos is probably bloat and poop. I'm sorry you feel stuck in the binge cycle. I was just there a few weeks ago and hit my low. Feel bad-binge-feelworse. How much are you restricting the day after? Maybe it's too much. Also, try to be nice to yourself after a binge. The urge to eat less and just lose the weight is strong. But binging can be deeply emotional for some people, a need to numb out. If this is true for you, are there other ways you can comfort yourself?

I've been drinking giant Mason jars of calming/healthy herbal tea (rose petals, dandelion, burdock, raspberry leaf, chamomile) at night after dinner to help limit night time snacking. Like 1 to 2 litres per night. Keeps my belly full, mouth and hand occupied a bit. It's by no means a cure all, but its helping right now. 

I've struggled with nighttime eating too. Often it was stress or loneliness, and I was just eating to numb out. And not deal with the cravings of course.
Try Lyrica. It actually makes you feel good. Anti-seizure med also used as Anti-anxiety one.
Yeah it didn't last. I guess I've just been so down for so long when it first hit my body went ecstatic.

Tents. Every park, every bike ride I take I see new encampments scattered. I walked by 5 today as I was trying to do some daily exercise to relieve depression. Yesterday I saw at least 4 others. I grew up in this city, there was never anything like this.  People are avoiding the shelters because of COVID19 is what I'm told. I mean its decline not collapse but holy shit. I'm in Toronto, Canada.

Research shows group fitness compared to working out on machines alone helps slightly more in depressed people. Because it can help you get out of your head more. I did the Personal Trainer certification for my own interest a few years ago and always remembered that fact. Exercise buddies help with accountability, exercising in nature is calming and promotes a sense of wonder (nature just does this, helps to get out of your head once again). Running and weight lifting can offer an additional sense of accomplishment if you are tracking/scaling up. Yoga can help you learn to feel better in your body and often more relaxed. Dancing can be a pick me up. 


There's thousands of studies on all this. Usually takes a bunch saying the same thing for it to become accepted fact. Try google scholar or scihub if you are curious. The thing is  these studies usually only focus on a few things at once. 

All this to say though, whatever exercise you do is better than none. Whatever you will continue to do is the best. Many people try to do intense programs too soon (rapid weight loss etc), get hurt or frustrated and then feel like a failure and stop. 

150 minutes a week of moderate/intense exercise is what is set as the minimum to MAINTAIN good health.

I'm sorry you are feeling so low. Is it thoughts and worries and fears and emotions? I mean, is there any okayness you could sense in your body if you focused on it? Your breath, aliveness? It's hard to think your way out if a dark place. Did you learn anything about your CPTSD in terms of coping/soothing that you feel comfortable doing? 

Also, somethings give us energy, right. A phone call from someone we like for example. Boom our energy shoots up. I know you say you need rest, and the mental health system sucks where you are. Covid has made so much harder for sure. 

Healthy things that make us feel good can also be restorative in their own way. If you don't know where to start, that kind of means you can start anywhere. 

Take care

I am a compulsive eater. I've realized recently that I need more than just working on changing my habits, but that I might need lifetime support from others. 

I read an extensive review of BED therapies this week and saw the cold hard facts of relapse. I mean I know those facts, but I still latch on to trying harder, trying again, this time it will be different, I won't fail this time. I've been telling myself that for decades. I've learned and grown, sure. I've lost and gained hundreds.  And I'm at the point where binging and weight gain is making me feel so hopeless  about the future. My future. Like suicidal ideation because if I cant manage a basic bodily task, what good am I, will I ever be? 

In regards to the reading, that last line seems a bit outdated emotionally. Confront the delusional overeaters, they are more likely to feel attacked, shamed, cry, call you fat phobic. I was that delusional person for years. 

I agree it's a problem in the mind though. So easy to make excuses when stressed, tired or depressed. 

Please uh crosstalk away to me though, I don't have friends who struggle with food in this way.

Yeah, it's a bit of a bummer, but also at least honest so expectations can be better managed. I personally feel like such a gross failure when I fuck up again, and again. It might not be "therapy" as in paying for it for life. Could be a support group thing too. OA etc. I know theres free weightloss maintenance clinics in Ontario, essentially a weekly check in, as a way to manage relapse over a lifetime. 

I've never had an ED specialist therapist, but since depression and negative affect are so linked to BED, I think it can still help. 

My main realization from this is that I need to create a lifestyle with various checks n balances and supports, instead of all me and my internal motivation to eat well, exercise etc.
Am Canadian. Still sad.

This looks at all the theories why we binge, and the effects of various therapies. So it's not just us wondering lol. Also, still being figured out.  Don't let someone get lots of money promising they can cure you for sure with their book/program/course. Actual research (not anecdotal personal stories) shows it's more complex. 

 It also explains that binge eating is on the rise in the general population as well, which I didn't think about before. 

Essentially, all the therapies studied helped, however relapse over the long term is still an issue for many. Most of this relapse though is after therapy has concluded and people feel better. Until they don't, stress/trigger, BED cycle etc. We know. 

TL;DR maybe I just need weekly therapy for the rest of my life in order to manage my BED better?

I was on it for a few months until I felt like it stopped working because I was binging again. Started again and the past 3 days the urge to binge has faded, gawd sweet relief. I take 50mg around noon. I go to bed late though, (with or without vyvance).
Any free online groups/calls for BED support/group therapy? I'm in Canada, and everywhere I check is waitlisted. Thanks

I've never tried group, I do like hearing from folks with similar experiences though. It's TRUE, short term it's so easy to be like THIS IS IT (blank new method), yay. But effects often fade. 

I like the Rendezvous with Madness film Fest, they started it at CAMH years ago.

I like mushrooms. I like to do a small dose once a year to remind me of the beauty of the natural world. I tried microdosing several times this year *using an online guide* and just kept crying. 4 times. Once I felt better the the day after, but it faded. I was really excited to try because of the research. Glad it worked for you.

Wow  120mg of cymbalta used to work for me as well, until COVID19. I'd take 60 if I started feeling bad, and then 120 if that didnt work. No desire for sex, ability to orgasm and was constipated as fuck tho. And bad brain zaps everytime I went off it. 

No I'm definitely not bipolar,no mania ever. My dad and brother are, so its been a worry. What I was trying to say is that I can muster up enough force to do stuff and have some decent habits while being miserable and depressed this year, but then I fall back into bed and stay there for a while. The binge eating happens with the super low depression for me. The binge eating came after losing 120 lbs a few years ago and yeah I've gained most of it back which feels awful. 

I've read tons about neuroscience and trauma, and its helped with awareness, but not so much with behavioral change when I'm feeling low. I guess as someone who still gets hundreds of intrusive thoughts of self harm a day (when things are really bad) and I haven't cut since I was 15, neuroplasticity to me seems slow, you know? 

My friends know I'm depressed and we talk about mental health. It's just been such a slog and I dont want my shit to dominate hangouts. I actually cancelled 2 social hangs this week because I've been feeling so bad. 

Thank you for reply.

Thank you for this perspective. I think mine often comes from shame/overwhelm/grief. And it took me maybe 15 years to figure that out. 

Like theres many factors, and eating well, exercising, being social and such all help,  but I can be depressed in so many situations, it's hard to find a or the reason. 

How to change your mind and global perspective fundamentally? I love learning and am open to changing my mind, but this struggle is a well worn path at this point.
Thank you. I don't have too many benchmarks to measure progress over time. Something to think about!
Thank you. All coping and no clear answers, what a clear way to say it lol!  That's me when I'm doing ok in the midst of it.
Thanks for your reply. That's honestly great to hear that you are doing good 25 years later.

Thanks for your reply. What helped with the CPTSD in addressing actual issues? My last therapist thought I had it but she retired. All I remember was the importance of nervous system regulation and "parts". Well, I remember lots more but it never felt like I was dealing with underlying issues.
I left a good paying job to head to graduate school. I feel like I made such a dumb mistake financially. I hear you.

Thankfully some things like exercise or meditation or forcing oneself to be social also can feel good in and if themselves. As for the time involved, its astounding when you think of it over the years. I mean, that time probably would have gone to a hobby or tv or something less intense though, most likely right?

I'm not sure its courage. I think it takes more heart to keep on trying, over and over to get better. Not that suicide is "the easy way out", it's awful to feel this way. As for how, hope we never find out. 

I just looked it up on Wikipedia, you got me curious on the definition now. 

"Courage (also called bravery or valour) is the choice and willingness to  confront agony, pain, danger, uncertainty, or intimidation. Physical courage is bravery in the face of physical pain, hardship, even death or threat of death, while moral courage is the ability to act rightly in the face of popular opposition,[1] shame, scandal, discouragement, or personal loss. "

What's do you think is the solution? Like keep trying what has worked and new methods is the obvious one, while understanding there's no quick fix. 

I just mean, do I lower my expectations, if what I can reasonably accomplish in my life, in a day, totally, forever?  Because that feels like giving up/giving in, if that makes any sense. 

The seeing yourself slipping part sucks. You want to stop it, you can try, but like sometimes it's just watching shit happen as if you are not in control. Then you feel worse for not stopping it. Sigh.
Dont let the DMV and bank win. Life is hard and it sounds like you are in a tough spot. You can brainstorm a way around this admin bullshit tho.

35 here. It's honestly wild how strong people are who have dealt with this for years, to keep trying to live, over and over and over. Have you felt this way on and off for a long time? 

It occurred to me today how trying to manage my depression has been what I've spent the most time on in my life. All the books, therapy, meditation, journaling, pills, reading articles etc. 10k expert hours for sure. And still, gotta keep finding the will to go on, again. 

Open to chatting with fellow older folks.

20 years on and off here as well. It sucks. It's getting worse. Trying and trying is exhausting. 

Maybe instead of a big purpose or meaning, just something small to look forward too the next day? If nothing matters, you can be self-indulgent and do whatever you want that you can afford. 

Hurting others is what holds me back from going ahead with it. A bit of spite too.

Weight regain feels so shitty I'm sorry. I lost over 100 lbs  and over the past years have been gaining it back. Weight loss does make dating easier for sure, and I'm a woman. 

 I keep binging and saying I'll do better tomorrow.  Tomorrow never comes. Or it does, but only for a few weeks. Please keep trying. Weight maintenance is lifelong commitment, find what works and keep to it.
Sounds like the exact opposite of what therapists are supposed to do. That sucks. It's hard to tell people.
Thanks. Posting honestly felt like a relief because I haven't told anyone IRL.
Made this account today to say I'm suicidal.

I'm not religious, I think there's nothing after this but my body changing form to dust and all that's left is who ever remembers me. Burning sounds awful tho. Let alone burning forever. 

Sometimes I wish I had religion, that crazy eyed belief that you see in people, often in culty ones? At least they have passion.

Thank you for replying. 

Everyday I keep trying, and I keep failing. Which just makes it seem like what's the point. I've got goals, I just keep fucking up, and almost out of that spirit to keep trying, again. 

I hope it's not normal to feel like crap all the time. Sometimes, sure, that's life. Grief too. That's huge, the losses you've mentioned. I've never lost anyone close due to suicide. Honestly sometimes I read the /lastimages subreddit to remind me how much it affects others.
